The file looks correct. Here's a summary of what was wrong and what I fixed:

## Root Cause

The `"main"` field in `/home/chris/sites/glowing-robot/packages/design-system/package.json` was pointing to `dist/main.js`, but **that file doesn't exist**. Your Vite build (which uses `preserveModules: true`) actually outputs:

- `dist/main.cjs.js` — CommonJS format
- `dist/main.es.js` — ES Module format

When your Next.js app tried to resolve `@cw/design-system`, it found the package (the workspace symlink is correct ✓), but then couldn't load the entry point because `dist/main.js` was missing.

## Fix Applied

In `packages/design-system/package.json`:

```diff
- "main": "dist/main.js",
+ "main": "dist/main.cjs.js",
+ "module": "dist/main.es.js",
```

- **`main`** → points to the CJS bundle (`dist/main.cjs.js`) for Node/require resolution
- **`module`** → points to the ESM bundle (`dist/main.es.js`) for bundlers like Webpack/Next.js (this is what Next.js will prefer)

## Next Steps

1. **Rebuild the design system** to make sure the dist is fresh:
   ```bash
   yarn workspace @cw/design-system run build
   ```
2. **Restart your frontend dev server** so it picks up the corrected entry points:
   ```bash
   yarn cwoodley:fe:dev
   ```

The `exports` map is set up correctly. Here's what changed and why:

## What I Added

In `packages/design-system/package.json`, I added an `exports` field:

```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/main.es.js",
    "require": "./dist/main.cjs.js"
  },
  "./main.css": "./dist/design-system.css"
}
```

This tells modern bundlers (like Next.js/Webpack) exactly how to resolve each import path:

| Import | Resolves To |
|---|---|
| `@cw/design-system` | `./dist/main.es.js` (ESM) or `./dist/main.cjs.js` (CJS) |
| `@cw/design-system/main.css` | `./dist/design-system.css` |

The `exports` field takes **precedence** over `main`/`module`, so this is the most reliable way to map subpath imports like CSS files. Your existing `import "@cw/design-system/main.css"` in `layout.js` will now work without any changes.
